Job Posting: Environmental Scientist

State Water Resources Control Board

JC-539345



Environmental Scientist
  
ENVIRONMENTAL SCIENTIST

$4,551.00 - $9,787.00 per Month
  
New to State candidates will be hired into the minimum salary of the classification or minimum of alternate range when applicable.

**Final Filing Date:** **12/9/2026**

### **Job Description and Duties**

**Please note, the Water Boards do not participate in E-Verify.**

The Lahontan Water Board has an exciting employment opportunity in water quality protection. The Lahontan Water Board’s Nonpoint Source Unit has one opening for an Environmental Scientist (ES).

The incumbent ES will help protect water quality in the Lahontan Region by leading implementation of the region’s Nonpoint Source (NPS) Program. This includes NPS program management, Clean Water Act section 319 grants management, and implementation of permits and programs to manage impacts from rangeland and grazing operations.

Positions at the Water Boards may be eligible for a hybrid telework/in-office schedule based on the operational needs of the position. Applications will be accepted for individuals able to fulfill in-office duties from the Lahontan Water Board’s office in South Lake Tahoe.

Applicants should review the attached Duty Statement for more details about the position. Routine tasks include:

* Communicating with stakeholders, partners, and regulated entities
* Conducting meetings and field inspections
* Reviewing reports and tracking permit or project progress
* Data analysis and mapping
* Collaborating with other state and regional NPS programs
* Implementing outreach and education to the public, tribes, and regulated community
* Managing grants for projects to control NPS pollution
  

**Additional information:**

Candidates must possess essential personal qualifications including integrity, initiative, dependability, good judgment, the ability to work cooperatively with others, and the ability to perform the assigned duties of the class.

If the position requires driving, you must possess a current and valid driver’s license. Please Do Not include full Social Security Number, method of eligibility, and LEAP information in your application package.

Please let us know how you heard about this position by taking this brief survey: Recruitment Survey.

You will find additional information about the job in the **Duty Statement**.

### **Working Conditions**

**Positions at the Water Boards may be eligible for telework with in-person attendance based on the operational needs of the position****.**

**In accordance with the Statewide Telework Policy and GC 14200, the successful candidate must reside in California upon appointment. Proof of residency may be required.**

**Salary Information - CalHR salary rules allow appointment at the entrance rate (Cal. Code Regs., tit. 2, § 599.673) of a classification. For classes with alternate ranges, placement is based on education/experience. E****mployees appointed to** **the Attorney or Water Resource Control Engineer** **classification will receive Recruitment Higher Above Minimum (HAM) rate in accordance with the approved** **Civil Service Pay Scales.**

**In addition, note: Effective July 1, 2025, the State of California implemented the Personal Leave Program 2025 (PLP 2025) which reduces an employee’s monthly salary in exchange for leave credits. Employees appointed to this classification will have their monthly salary reduced and will accrue hours of PLP 2025 on the first day of each pay period in accordance with the applicable** **bargaining contract.** **The salary range(s) included on this job posting do not reflect the reduction in pay.**

  

### **Position Details**

JC-539345

### **Department Information**

The State Water Resources Control Board (SWRCB) and the nine (9) Regional Water Quality Control Boards (RWQCB) (collectively the Water Boards) work to preserve, enhance, and restore the quality of California’s water resources and drinking water for the protection of the environment, public health, and all beneficial uses, and to ensure proper water resource allocation and efficient use, for the benefit of present and future generations.

The Water Boards value diversity, equity, and inclusion throughout the organization. We foster an environment where employees from a variety of backgrounds, cultures, and personal experiences are welcomed and can thrive. We believe the diversity of our employees is essential to inspiring innovative solutions. jobs.title: GHD Graduate Program 2026/27 – Environmental Science (Planning/Impact Assessment) – Melbourne
jobs.description:
**We’re GHD.**

We don’t do hair. But we do straighten out some of the world’s biggest challenges.

We’re engineers, scientists, designers, architects, planners, advisors, innovators and change makers, committed to making energy, water and communities sustainable for generations to come.

Since 1928, we’ve been wholly owned by our employees. Today, we are 11,000 diverse and skilled individuals working in over 160 offices across five continents — Asia, Australia, Europe, North and South America, and the Pacific region.

  

Who could you be at GHD?

Our **Planning & Impact Assessment team** based in **Melbourne** supports projects through the environmental planning and approvals process, helping identify and manage environmental impacts and risks. The team brings together environmental scientists, planners, engineers and environmental specialists to support projects through assessment, approvals and delivery.

The team is looking for a **Graduate Environmental Scientist** to join our Graduate cohort, commencing in either **February** or **July 2027** .

We’re looking for someone who:

* has recently graduated (or is a current student expecting to graduate by the end of 2026, or mid-2027) with a degree in **Environmental Science, or a related environmental discipline**
* has an interest in **environmental planning, impact assessment and environmental approvals**
* is keen to develop experience in environmental investigations, data collection and analysis, environmental impact assessments and technical reporting
* has an interest in understanding environmental risks, regulatory requirements and sustainable project outcomes
* has great verbal and written communication skills and enjoys working collaboratively in a multidisciplinary environment.
  

Our two-year Graduate Development Program is designed to give you a smooth start to your consulting career. Alongside your peers, managers and mentors, we’ll help you detangle any challenges along the way. You’ll be mentored by senior aquatic ecologists with decades of experience across Australia, and build skills in survey techniques, field safety, animal ethics requirements and technical reporting that will set you up for a long career in aquatic science.

**A frizz-free application process:**

#WeDontDoHair but we do want your journey to be as smooth as possible, so here’s everything you need to help you prep like a pro:

* **Your CV:** This gives us a snapshot of what you’ve studied and your experiences, both paid and unpaid.
* **A cover letter:** Think of this as your chance to show us where you’d love to grow within GHD, while letting your communication skills shine.
* **Your transcript:** This helps us understand what you’ve been learning, from your core subjects to the electives that sparked your curiosity.

**Your journey to joining GHD:**

Here’s what to expect, step by step:

* **Screening:** We review applications as they come in, but be mindful that the bulk of our screening happens after applications close, so don’t worry if you don’t hear from us right away.
* **Virtual Assessments:** If you make it through the first stage, you’ll record some answers to a few straightforward questions and complete some cognitive games. This helps us get a better sense of your work style and alignment to GHD
* **Meet the team:** If you’re successful, you’ll have a face-to-face interview (wherever possible) with your prospective team. We’ll chat through some behavioural questions to learn more about your skills and experience. It ’ s also a chance for you to get to know us!
* **Offer:** Congratulations! We’ll talk through all the finer details, like salary, your start date, our onboarding process and what to expect before your first day.

We’re committed to being as inclusive as possible and giving everyone an equitable chance of getting through our application process. **If you identify as someone who is neurodiverse or have a disability** and need adjustments to any part of the process, let us know in your application form—we’re here to help.

  

**Ready to shine?**

If you’ve got your documents polished and prepped, the application should only take 10-15 minutes. Apply now and take the first step toward an exciting career in consulting.

**If you’ve previously applied for this position, there’s no need to reapply.**

**GHD: The Power of Commitment**

At GHD, we don’t just believe in the power of commitment, we live and breathe it every day.

Community impact is important to us, influencing how we work, our projects and how we give back. Our *GHD in the Community* program partners with not-for-profit organisations so that we can work on pro-bono projects, as well as volunteering and fundraising for philanthropic and humanitarian causes. As a business, we also channel some of our profits into the *GHD Foundation* *,* a registered charity that addresses disadvantage and inequality in children accessing STEAM education in the countries where we live and work.

Within GHD, our employee groups and networks help us foster community, find our tribe, and celebrate what makes us unique. These groups play a big part in our global diversity, equity and inclusion strategy, creating spaces for meaningful and safe conversations, connecting with likeminded individuals, and creating a voice to leadership.

**Environmental Health Assistant**
==================================

Reserve

In-service title: Preventative Medicine Technician

As a part-time Environmental Health Assistant, you’ll be responsible for providing healthcare to support and maintain the health and wellbeing of Army members. You’ll work in and around Army camps minimising the risks posed by climate, non-combat injuries, unsanitary conditions and vector-borne diseases.

If you’re looking to experience adventure and excitement outside the everyday, earn tax-free pay and work as part of a close-knit team, this is an exciting opportunity that can work around your lifestyle.

  

Service Type

Reserve

View Full-time role

Entry Method

Exciting part-time role

General Entry: Non-technical Reserve

Salary

You'll be paid to train and on completion of your Initial Military Training and Initial Employment Training, you’ll earn a tax-free daily rate of at least:

Your daily rate while training

from

$170per day

Your daily rate once trained

from

$223per day

Plus generous financial benefits

  

### **What you'll do**

Your day-to-day

You’ll assist commanders in the prevention and control of disease and non-battle injuries to ensure ADF members can maintain a high level of health and fitness to carry out their duties.

Your training will equip you with the skills to study and assess environmental and occupational health threats, then implement effective control procedures.

Your duties may include:

* assessing environmental and occupational health threats by gathering and evaluating information obtained through health intelligence sources, on-site surveys and health surveillance
* determining and implementing counter measures to minimise the environmental and occupational health threats including vector/pest control, water quality analysis, food safety, waste management and sanitation
* conducting health surveillance and using health surveillance data to assess effectiveness of counter measures and plan investigations and health surveys
* conducting surveys and performing testing to assess environmental and occupational health threats and counter measures during deployment
* advising on the full range of Environmental Health Assistant issues to medical and non-medical personnel to help promote health and prevent casualties.

How you'll progress

Opportunities for progression and upskilling continue throughout your career. As you progress, the Army will provide you with development opportunities to assist you with your increasing leadership responsibility, as well as further education and specialised training to strengthen your skillset. This will help you to command and run a highly skilled team of soldiers and the employment of their equipment.

Where you'll work

The Army Reserve has units located all across Australia and offers you the flexibility to serve where you live. There are training locations in cities, small towns and regional areas. Even if there isn’t a unit close to you there may be other ways to serve. You’ll have a Careers Coach who you can ask about your options.

Part-time Environmental Health Assistant vacancies are currently restricted to applicants who reside within 90 minutes of Edinburgh, SA; Oakleigh, VIC; or Enoggera, QLD.

Age

You can apply for a role in the ADF from 16.5 years of age and must be at least 17 to join. For Reserve service, the maximum age to apply is 60 years, with a Compulsory Retirement Age (CRA) of 65. Candidates who wish to enlist into the Reserves beyond the age of 61 years will need further assessment to ensure they can complete all pre-requisite training in their chosen field prior to reaching CRA.

You don’t need a driver’s licence for this role but if you have one, it can’t be suspended or cancelled.

Security requirements

All ADF members require a security clearance. As an ADF member, you’ll need to obtain the appropriate level of security clearance for your role. You’ll need a collection of relevant information including background checks and/or interviews so the Australian Government Security Vetting Agency (AGSVA) can make an informed assessment to ensure the protection of Government resources and information. Your Careers Coach will explain what level of clearance is required for the career you are considering.

For more information or to learn about how security clearance will apply to you, view the eligibility requirements page.

Education and experience

Completion of Year 10 (or equivalent) education required with passes in English and Maths. If you haven't completed Year 10 but are interested in joining, the ADF may be able to support your application. Employment history and other qualifications will be considered. You’ll have a Careers Coach who you can speak to about your options.

Health and fitness

To join the ADF, you must be healthy and physically fit. This is partially assessed from the completion of an extensive questionnaire covering your medical history, followed by a physical examination.

You’ll also be required to successfully pass a physical fitness assessment.

### **What you'll do**

Your day-to-day

You’ll identify hazards, assess exposure and health risks, recommend and evaluate controls and provide evidence-based advice to protect ADF personnel and support operational capability.

In the field, you’ll provide and implement practical environmental health controls in support of air operations. This includes assessing and managing risks across deployed airfields, accommodation areas and temporary facilities with a focus on field hygiene, potable water, waste management, vector control and occupational health hazards. You may also support humanitarian assistance and disaster relief operations by protecting deployed forces, partner agencies and affected populations.

Your duties may include:

* health threat assessments
* epidemiological studies
* field hygiene and sanitation
* water quality testing, analysis, treatment and advice
* pest/vector management and control
* chemical, biological, radiological, nuclear defence (CBRND) assessments and advice
* disaster support and emergency management
* workplace and accommodation assessments
* operational health support and planning
* occupational hygiene assessments
* preventive health education

How you'll progress

Opportunities for progression and upskilling continue throughout your career as an officer. As you progress, the Air Force will provide you with leadership, management and communications training to develop your ability to effectively manage your teams. You’ll also be provided with training opportunities to further develop your role-related skills. This world-class training will strengthen your skillset and enable you to become an influential leader in the Air Force.

As an officer in the Air Force, you may also undertake a posting to an Any Officer role during your career, such as instructor/training roles and staff officer roles. This experience helps you broaden your skill set and prepare for more senior roles.

Where you'll work

Following training, you may be posted to any Air Force base or Defence establishment within Australia or possibly overseas, although overseas postings are limited.

You will normally be employed in health support environments. However, your duties and skills may take you to all areas of ADF operations, both locally and overseas.

**Environmental Health Manager**
================================

Reserve

In-service title: Environmental Health Officer

As a part-time Environmental Health Manager, you’ll be an important member of the health strategy team to maintain the health of the Army. You’ll provide essential support to command in barracks, in the field and on operations.

If you’re looking to experience adventure and excitement outside the everyday, earn tax-free pay and work as part of a close-knit team, this is an exciting opportunity that can work around your lifestyle.

  

Service Type

Reserve

Your daily rate while training

from

$216per day

from

$274per day

Plus generous financial benefits

  

### **What you'll do**

Your day-to-day

You’ll be responsible for the planning, identification, evaluation and recommendations of control strategies to minimise environmental and workplace health impacts on ADF members.

In the field, you’ll ensure high environmental health and sanitation standards, that are appropriate for the situation you’re in. This may include not only providing advice but sometimes physically implementing control strategies (pest control, construction and maintenance of field hygiene facilities, etc). You may also be employed in disaster support, providing advice and support to deployed forces and affected populations.

Your duties may include:

* **advice to commanders –** combination of advice related to prevention of disease, active monitoring of environments, hazard management, and mitigation strategies and recommendations
* **human resource management –** managing Environmental Health Teams
* **water supplies –** providing advice on the safety and quality of all Army water supplies, including reticulated base supplies, field water supplies and swimming pools
* **food safety –** advising on the safety and quality of all Army food supplies including procurement, delivery, storage, preparation and serving
* **facilities –** determining that appropriate standards are applied to Army facilities to meet health and safety requirements and that facilities are being maintained in a sanitary and safe condition
* **work health and safety –** monitoring and evaluation of the Army working environment, providing recommendations for the control of workplace hazards including risk analysis
* **disease control –** implementing measures for the prevention and control of communicable disease and maintaining and interpreting disease statistics and other epidemiological data
* **waste disposal –** advising on the safe disposal of human, perishable and industrial wastes in accordance with compliance with appropriate environmental standards
* **pest control –** management and advice on the safe eradication of pests and vermin
* **vector control –** management and programs for the effective control of vector borne diseases
* **operational health support –** providing advice and preventative medicine services for hygiene and sanitation in field operations
* **disaster support –** maintaining public health standards in support of disaster preparedness and disaster recovery
* **liaison –** liaising with civilian environmental health and other specialist authorities.

How you'll progress

Opportunities for progression and upskilling continue throughout your career as an officer. As you progress, the Army will provide you with leadership, management, and specialist skills training to develop your ability to effectively manage your teams. You’ll also be provided with training opportunities to further develop your role-related expertise. This world-class training will strengthen your skillset and enable you to become an influential leader in the Army.

As an officer in the Army, you may also undertake a posting to an Any Officer role during your career, such as instructor/training roles and staff officer roles. This experience helps you broaden your skill set and prepare for more senior roles.

Where you'll work

The Army Reserve has units located all across Australia and offers you the flexibility to serve where you live. There are training locations in cities, small towns and regional areas. Even if there isn’t a unit close to you there may be other ways to serve. You’ll have a Careers Coach who you can ask about your options.

You’ll most likely be located at one of the Health Battalions in Adelaide, Brisbane, Darwin or Townsville. You’ll work with and lead small teams in both field and deployment locations (exercises and operations).

Citizenship

You can apply for a role in the ADF from 16.5 years of age and must be at least 17 to join. For Reserve service, the maximum age to apply is 60 years, with a Compulsory Retirement Age (CRA) of 65. ### **What you'll do**

Your day-to-day

You’ll assist commanders in the prevention and control of disease and non-battle injuries to ensure ADF members can maintain a high level of health and fitness to carry out their duties.

Your training will equip you with the skills to study and assess environmental and occupational health threats, then implement effective control procedures.

Your duties may include:

* assessing environmental and occupational health threats by gathering and evaluating information obtained through health intelligence sources, on-site surveys and health surveillance
* determining and implementing counter measures to minimise the environmental and occupational health threats including vector/pest control, water quality analysis, food safety, waste management and sanitation
* conducting health surveillance and using health surveillance data to assess effectiveness of counter measures and plan investigations and health surveys
* conducting surveys and performing testing to assess environmental and occupational health threats and counter measures during deployment
* advising on the full range of Environmental Health Assistant issues to medical and non-medical personnel to help promote health and prevent casualties.

How you'll progress

Opportunities for progression and upskilling continue throughout your career. As you progress, the Army will provide you with development opportunities to assist you with your increasing leadership responsibility, as well as further education and specialised training to strengthen your skillset. This will help you to command and run a highly skilled team of soldiers and the employment of their equipment.

Where you'll work

The Army Reserve has units located all across Australia and offers you the flexibility to serve where you live. There are training locations in cities, small towns and regional areas. Even if there isn’t a unit close to you there may be other ways to serve. You’ll have a Careers Coach who you can ask about your options.

Part-time Environmental Health Assistant vacancies are currently restricted to applicants who reside within 90 minutes of Edinburgh, SA; Oakleigh, VIC; or Enoggera, QLD.

### **What you'll do**

Your day-to-day

You’ll identify hazards, assess exposure and health risks, recommend and evaluate controls and provide evidence-based advice to protect ADF personnel and support operational capability.

In the field, you’ll provide and implement practical environmental health controls in support of air operations. This includes assessing and managing risks across deployed airfields, accommodation areas and temporary facilities with a focus on field hygiene, potable water, waste management, vector control and occupational health hazards. You may also support humanitarian assistance and disaster relief operations by protecting deployed forces, partner agencies and affected populations.

Your duties may include:

* health threat assessments
* epidemiological studies
* field hygiene and sanitation
* water quality testing, analysis, treatment and advice
* pest/vector management and control
* chemical, biological, radiological, nuclear defence (CBRND) assessments and advice
* disaster support and emergency management
* workplace and accommodation assessments
* operational health support and planning
* occupational hygiene assessments
* preventive health education

How you'll progress

Opportunities for progression and upskilling continue throughout your career as an officer. As you progress, the Air Force will provide you with leadership, management and communications training to develop your ability to effectively manage your teams. You’ll also be provided with training opportunities to further develop your role-related skills. This world-class training will strengthen your skillset and enable you to become an influential leader in the Air Force.

As an officer in the Air Force, you may also undertake a posting to an Any Officer role during your career, such as instructor/training roles and staff officer roles. This experience helps you broaden your skill set and prepare for more senior roles.

Where you'll work

Following training, you may be posted to any Air Force base or Defence establishment within Australia or possibly overseas, although overseas postings are limited.

You will normally be employed in health support environments. However, your duties and skills may take you to all areas of ADF operations, both locally and overseas.

If you’re looking to experience adventure and excitement outside the everyday, earn tax-free pay and work as part of a close-knit team, this is an exciting opportunity that can work around your lifestyle.

### **What you'll do**

Your day-to-day

You’ll be responsible for the planning, identification, evaluation and recommendations of control strategies to minimise environmental and workplace health impacts on ADF members.

In the field, you’ll ensure high environmental health and sanitation standards, that are appropriate for the situation you’re in. This may include not only providing advice but sometimes physically implementing control strategies (pest control, construction and maintenance of field hygiene facilities, etc). You may also be employed in disaster support, providing advice and support to deployed forces and affected populations.

Your duties may include:

* **advice to commanders –** combination of advice related to prevention of disease, active monitoring of environments, hazard management, and mitigation strategies and recommendations
* **human resource management –** managing Environmental Health Teams
* **water supplies –** providing advice on the safety and quality of all Army water supplies, including reticulated base supplies, field water supplies and swimming pools
* **food safety –** advising on the safety and quality of all Army food supplies including procurement, delivery, storage, preparation and serving
* **facilities –** determining that appropriate standards are applied to Army facilities to meet health and safety requirements and that facilities are being maintained in a sanitary and safe condition
* **work health and safety –** monitoring and evaluation of the Army working environment, providing recommendations for the control of workplace hazards including risk analysis
* **disease control –** implementing measures for the prevention and control of communicable disease and maintaining and interpreting disease statistics and other epidemiological data
* **waste disposal –** advising on the safe disposal of human, perishable and industrial wastes in accordance with compliance with appropriate environmental standards
* **pest control –** management and advice on the safe eradication of pests and vermin
* **vector control –** management and programs for the effective control of vector borne diseases
* **operational health support –** providing advice and preventative medicine services for hygiene and sanitation in field operations
* **disaster support –** maintaining public health standards in support of disaster preparedness and disaster recovery
* **liaison –** liaising with civilian environmental health and other specialist authorities.

How you'll progress

Opportunities for progression and upskilling continue throughout your career as an officer. As you progress, the Army will provide you with leadership, management, and specialist skills training to develop your ability to effectively manage your teams. You’ll also be provided with training opportunities to further develop your role-related expertise. This world-class training will strengthen your skillset and enable you to become an influential leader in the Army.

As an officer in the Army, you may also undertake a posting to an Any Officer role during your career, such as instructor/training roles and staff officer roles. This experience helps you broaden your skill set and prepare for more senior roles.

Where you'll work

The Army Reserve has units located all across Australia and offers you the flexibility to serve where you live. There are training locations in cities, small towns and regional areas. Even if there isn’t a unit close to you there may be other ways to serve. You’ll have a Careers Coach who you can ask about your options.

You’ll most likely be located at one of the Health Battalions in Adelaide, Brisbane, Darwin or Townsville. You’ll work with and lead small teams in both field and deployment locations (exercises and operations).
